title: Who kept watch for Jehoiada’s plan: “priests and … Levites … porters of the doors” (2 Chronicles 23:4) or “the captains” and “the guard” (2 Kings 11:5-8)
summary: Jehoiada’s order to the sabbath watch in 2 Chronicles 23:4-7 addresses priests and Levites, who are to be porters of the doors and compass the king. The same order in 2 Kings 11:5-8 is addressed to the captains and the guard, who keep the watch of the king’s house and compass the king.
text: KJV 2 Chronicles 23:4: “This is the thing that ye shall do; A third part of you entering on the sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, shall be porters of the doors;” KJV 2 Chronicles 23:7: “And the Levites shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand; and whosoever else cometh into the house, he shall be put to death: but be ye with the king when he cometh in, and when he goeth out.” KJV 2 Kings 11:5: “And he commanded them, saying, This is the thing that ye shall do; A third part of you that enter in on the sabbath shall even be keepers of the watch of the king's house;” KJV 2 Kings 11:8: “And ye shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand: and he that cometh within the ranges, let him be slain: and be ye with the king as he goeth out and as he cometh in.” Hebrew (WLC) 23:4: זֶ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֨ית מִכֶּ֜ם בָּאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֗ת לַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ וְלַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְשֹֽׁעֲרֵ֖י הַסִּפִּֽים׃ Hebrew (WLC) 11:5: וַיְצַוֵּ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר זֶ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשׂ֑וּן הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֤ית מִכֶּם֙ בָּאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת וְשֹׁ֣מְרֵ֔י מִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/14/23/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/11/.

In Chronicles the thirds are porters of the doors (priests and Levites), the king’s house, and the gate of the foundation, and the Levites compass the king. text: KJV 2 Chronicles 27:8: “He was five and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.” Hebrew (WLC) 27:8: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְחָמֵ֛שׁ שָׁנָ֖ה הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכֹ֑ו וְשֵׁשׁ־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ Brenton’s Greek page (2 Chronicles 27) prints the verse labels 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9, and prints no label 8. [The page runs from the acts of Jotham at verse 7 straight to his death at verse 9.] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/14/27/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2CH27.htm.
reasoning: The KJV and the Hebrew edition quoted have a verse 8 giving Jotham’s age of twenty-five and sixteen years in Jerusalem, repeating verse 1. The Greek page prints no label 8 between the book of the kings at verse 7 and Jotham’s death at verse 9.
scope: T applies at 2 Chronicles 27:8 and only to the verse. This is a statement about one printed edition of the Greek; it does not show that no Greek manuscript has the verse, and the record does not say why the page prints no verse 8. The verse repeats a statement made in 27:1 and the record does not treat the repetition as a problem in either text. The cited Greek page prints verse labels 1 to 7 and 9. This compares the wording of the texts quoted. It does not show which wording is original. The book is a history written in prose; the comparison is of what the texts print, not of why the writer worded it so. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek quoted is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original, and the record does not claim the Greek is a mistranslation of the Hebrew. English in square brackets is the researcher’s plain rendering, not a KJV quotation and not a lexicon entry.
